name: tma_store_loaded
extends: protocol-v4.json (R1, installed) — new question: the destination of a TMA store
mechanisms: memory.store_l2 / memory.shared_service (read only: which installed rate binds)
data_seen_before_writing: Per-PC hardware sampling and engine journals (fg-line-sync/jr24): DGF-KG-FP8-TN-R05 waits about 930 cycles per 16 KiB epilogue sub-block on DEPBAR.LE SB0,1 after UTMAREDG.2D.ADD (engine 100-330); FIF-BS-SM103-NVF4-C05 693 against 303 per 16 KiB UTMASTG; CUF-DSL-DENSE-PERSIST-C04 210 against 31 per 8 KiB. The single-cluster captures of the same kernels are accurate (0.92-1.08), the full-GPU ones are not (0.50-0.92). Hardware counters (fg-fa3/hwmet/bw-metrics.tsv): DGF-KG-FP8-TN-R01 reduce sectors 188.7 MB, lts__d_sectors_fill_device = dram__bytes_read = 138.8 MB (the reduce destination is fetched from DRAM), DRAM throughput 53.7 % of peak; CUF-DSL-DENSE-PERSIST-C04 writes 55 MB and reads 5.4 MB from DRAM (plain stores do not fetch). Engine: a reduce store fetches non-resident sectors through the shared DRAM read service but the bulk group completes without waiting for the fetch; store_round r3 (ring destination, 8 KiB): 257.0 at one SM, 290.1 (b300) / 520.3 (h100) at all SMs. No cell of this version has been run.
question: When does a TMA store group complete as a function of (1) plain store or reduce-add, (2) a destination that stays in L2 (ring of 4 boxes per CTA) or a fresh box every round that is not in L2, (3) one SM or all SMs?
probe: probe/store_dest.cu: N CTAs (one per SM, 128 threads); round = bar.sync ; thread 0: UTMASTG or UTMAREDG.add of one box + commit_group + wait_group.read <STAGES-1> ; bar.sync. Source boxes written and fenced once. Before every launch the host clears the destination and writes an eviction buffer of --evict-mib MiB (2048 unless stated). 264 rounds, first 8 not counted, 8 launches after a discarded one, runs a and b. Period per CTA = cycles / round.
cells: run_dest.sh, 26 cells per run: box 16384: red {0,1} x fresh {0,1} x stages {2,4} x N {1, all SMs}; box 8192: red {0,1} x fresh {0,1} x stages 2 x N {1, all}; no eviction (evict-mib 0): red {0,1}, fresh 1, stages 2, N 1, box 16384. ncu counters (b300 only, run_dest_ncu.sh): the four N = all, stages 2, box 16384 cells with dram__bytes_read.sum, dram__bytes_write.sum, lts__d_sectors_fill_device.sum, lts__t_sectors_op_red.sum, lts__t_sectors_op_write.sum, sm__cycles_active.max (--cache-control none: the probe evicts by itself).
sass_gate: sass_check_dest.py: each of the four k_dest<RED, STAGES> has, in the round loop, exactly one UTMASTG (RED 0) or one UTMAREDG (RED 1) and none of the other, one UTMACMDFLUSH, one DEPBAR.LE SB0, <STAGES-1>, two BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80, no STS, no clock read other than the single predicated one that starts the counted window.
units: S = box bytes / installed store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle (b300 32.19, h100 31.65): 509 / 518 cycles per 16 KiB. W = box bytes x SMs / installed l2_write_bytes_per_ns in cycles (b300 8038 B/ns at the measured SM clock, 148 SMs: about 579; h100 3965 B/ns, 132 SMs: about 983). Rd = the same with dram_read_bytes_per_ns (b300 7324: about 636; h100 3231: about 1206).

predictions.control_C1: plain, ring, N = 1: S within 5 % (store_round measured 257.0 per 8 KiB on both devices).
predictions.control_C2: plain, ring, all SMs: 2 x the store_round value (580 b300, 1040 h100) within 8 %.
predictions.plain_fresh: equal to plain ring within 8 % at one SM and at all SMs (a plain store does not fetch its destination; counters of CUF-DSL-DENSE-PERSIST-C04). If it is slower by more than 8 % the destination matters for plain stores too and the excess is tabulated.
predictions.reduce_ring: equal to plain ring within 8 % (destination resident, nothing to fetch).
predictions.reduce_fresh_engine_today: equal to plain fresh (the group does not wait for the fetch).
predictions.reduce_fresh_candidates: at all SMs, period per 16 KiB: (a) W (write service only); (b) max(W, Rd) (completion waits for the fetch, fetch and write overlap); (c) W + Rd (fetch then write, serial per sector); (d) 2 W (a reduce takes the write service twice). At one SM none of the shared services binds: (b)-(d) predict S plus at most the DRAM latency once.
predictions.no_eviction: with evict-mib 0 the cleared destination of the one-SM fresh cells is still in L2 (4.2 MB): reduce fresh = reduce ring within 8 %; this is the check that the eviction buffer, not the address pattern, makes the destination non-resident.

decision: The reduce rule is the candidate whose all-SM prediction is within 10 % of the measured reduce-fresh period on a device, for box 16384 and 8192 and both STAGES, with runs a / b within 5 %; b300 counters must show dram__bytes_read within 20 % of the reduced bytes for reduce fresh and under 10 % of them for reduce ring and plain fresh. If no candidate fits, or two fit, nothing is installed and the table is recorded. Full-GPU error is not used.
rule_forms: (b): the bulk group of a reduce store completes no earlier than the last RMW fetch of its sectors (engine: fill_done of MemoryHierarchy::store joins the completion; no new leaf). (c) / (d): additionally the reduce sector occupies the shared L2-write service after its fetch / twice (engine rule on the reduce path; no new value). Any of these touches memory-hierarchy service rules that the shared-memory line owns: it is implemented only on the reduce / TMA-store completion path and reported to that line before merging.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no candidate added after data without an addendum that says the data was seen.

addenda.after_run: store-dest b300-r1 (GPU-ca40cb09) and h100-r1 (GPU-ebc96a9f): 26 cells x 2 runs each, SASS gate 4 / 4, runs a / b within 1.4 %; b300 ncu counters for the four all-SM cells
addenda.table_cycles_per_16KiB: b300 one SM | 148 SMs | h100 one SM | 132 SMs: plain ring 512.9 | 534.8 | 512.9 | 1075; plain fresh 512.9 | 610.2 | 512.9 | 1303; reduce ring 640.9 | 675.4 | 640.9 | 1381; reduce fresh 640.9 | 1570 | 640.9 | 3796. The 8 KiB cells are half of these within 1 %; STAGES 2 and 4 agree within 1 %; the one-SM fresh cells are the same with and without the eviction buffer. All-SM cells spread across SMs (p10-p90) by 10-30 %.
addenda.counters_b300_all_SMs: 640 MB stored per cell. reduce fresh: dram__bytes_read 640 MB, dram__bytes_write 639 MB, fill_device 640 MB; plain fresh: read 0.02 MB, write 639 MB; reduce ring: read 9.7 MB, write 14 MB; plain ring: read 0.02 MB, write 16 MB. A reduce onto a destination that is not in L2 fetches every byte from DRAM; a plain store never fetches; fresh destinations are written back to DRAM within the run.
addenda.declared_checks: C1 holds (512.9 against S = 509 / 518). C2 holds (534.8 against 580, -7.8 %; 1075 against 1040). plain_fresh fails: +14 % (b300) and +21 % (h100) over the ring at all SMs (equal at one SM): tabulated; h100 1303 is the installed DRAM write rate (1328), b300 610 the installed L2 write rate (613). reduce_ring fails: a reduce is 1.25 x a plain store on one SM (640.9 / 512.9 = 1.2496 on both devices, both box sizes, ring and fresh) and 1.26-1.29 x at all SMs. reduce_fresh at all SMs: none of the four candidates is within 10 % (b300 1570 against W 613, max(W, Rd) 673, W + Rd 1286, 2 W 1226; h100 3796 against 1080, 1325, 2405, 2160). no_eviction: uninformative, one SM never binds a shared service. By the decision rule nothing is installed.
addenda.reading_after_data: (1) Measured, both devices, no free parameter: a reduce sector occupies its SM's store port 1.25 times as long as a plain sector. (2) The engine today completes a reduce group without waiting for the fetch of its destination; hardware at all SMs is 2.3 x (b300) and 2.8 x (h100) slower with a fresh destination than with a resident one, and the counters show the fetch is the only difference. (3) The all-SM fresh-reduce period corresponds to a total DRAM traffic (read + write-back) of 6.3 TB/s on b300 and 2.3 TB/s on h100, 86-89 % and 70 % of the installed one-direction DRAM rates: reads and write-backs share DRAM and the mix is slower than either alone on h100. Not derived here: how the DRAM budget is split under a read / write mix (a shared-service rule, owned by the shared-memory line).
addenda.next: Tracer captures of eight cells per device (red x fresh x {1, all SMs}, 16 KiB, STAGES 2) replayed through the engine before any rule: the replay shows what the installed fetch path already gives once the group completion waits for it. Rule forms to evaluate on the replay, written after the data: (i) reduce sectors occupy the per-SM store port 1.25 x (value measured here); (ii) the bulk group of a reduce store completes no earlier than the last DRAM fetch of its sectors. Neither changes an L2 / DRAM service rate.

addenda.name: placement
addenda.text: Written before any placement cell is run. Question (asked by the user before any rule about the fetch is kept): does the cost of a reduce store onto a non-resident destination depend on which GPCs the storing SMs are in? Probe change: store_dest takes --active-file (SM ids); the grid still covers every SM, CTAs on other SMs only take part in the start handshake; the per-SM period is written out. SM sets from configs/hardware/<device>/sm_topology.json (gpc column), gpc_sets.py: `one` = every SM of the largest GPC (b300 20, h100 18), `spread` = the same number taken evenly from all GPCs, `halfgpc` = whole GPCs up to about half the SMs (64 on both devices: four GPCs), `halfeach` = the same number, 8 per GPC, `all`. Cells (run_dest_gpc.sh, 9 per run, 16 KiB, STAGES 2): reduce + fresh on the five sets; reduce + ring on one / spread; plain + fresh on halfgpc / halfeach. Reading, fixed here: R1 = period(one) / period(spread) and R2 = period(halfgpc) / period(halfeach), medians over the active SMs, for reduce + fresh. Both inside 0.92-1.08 on both runs: the fetch does not depend on the GPC (card-wide resource). Either above 1.15 on both runs: it is GPC-scoped. Anything between: unclear, reported as such. Additional view for `all`: per-GPC medians of the per-SM periods against the spread inside a GPC; a between-GPC range larger than twice the median within-GPC range is reported as a placement effect. The reduce + ring and plain + fresh pairs are read the same way for the write path alone. Nothing is installed from these cells.

addenda.name: placement_result
addenda.after_run: store-dest-gpc b300-r1 (GPU-052994e4) and h100-r1 (GPU-2dd7c2cc), 9 cells x 2 runs, SASS gate 4 / 4
addenda.text: Median period per 16 KiB over the active SMs. b300: reduce + fresh one GPC (20 SMs) 679.6, spread 640.9 (R1 1.060 on both runs); whole GPCs (64 SMs) 732.5, 8 per GPC 674.2 (R2 1.086 / 1.085); all SMs 1562. reduce + ring one GPC 676.6 against spread 640.9; plain + fresh whole GPCs 535.0 against 513.0. h100: reduce + fresh one GPC (18 SMs) 938.5, spread 640.9 (R1 1.464 / 1.469); whole GPCs 1656 / 1694, 8 per GPC 1567 / 1545 (R2 1.057 / 1.096); all 3777 / 3600. reduce + ring one GPC 1110.7 against spread 640.9 (1.73); plain + fresh whole GPCs 744 against 607 (1.22). By the reading fixed before the run: h100 is GPC-scoped (R1 above 1.15 on both runs); b300 is 'unclear' by the ratios (R2 just above 1.08) and shows a placement effect in the all-SM view (per-GPC medians 1055 for the 10-SM GPC against 1453-1583 for the others: between-GPC range 528, more than twice the median within-GPC range 210). The effect is at least as large without any fetch (ring destination) as with it: it belongs to the store path of the SMs of one GPC, not to the destination fetch alone. Nothing installed; the question of how the engine should scope the store / fetch service is left open.

addenda.name: gpc_scope
addenda.written: before any data of these cells, by the shared-memory line that took this question over (the shared-memory line that took this question over); seen before writing: the placement cells above and the cp.async cells of l2_merge protocol-v2 merge_mechanics_rerun_result
addenda.text: Question: the limit of the store service and of the L2 read service per GPC and per card. Seen: storing SMs of one whole GPC reach about 0.8 TB/s plain and 0.53-0.62 TB/s reduce on h100 (16-18 SMs; unlimited would be 1.0 / 0.8) and about 1.1 / 0.94 on b300; 64 storing SMs spread over the GPCs reach 3.5 / 4.2 TB/s on the card; unshared cp.async reads reach 1.05 / 2.7 TB/s per GPC and 7.2 / 19.2 TB/s on the card. Cells (run_scope.sh; SM sets from scope_sets.py with the topology table's gpc column; two runs): g1k2 g1k4 g1k8 g1k12 g1kall = the first k SMs of the largest GPC, ek1 ek2 ek4 ek8 ekall = the first k SMs of every GPC; for each set a plain TMA store ring and a reduce store ring (store_dest, 16 KiB boxes, destination resident) and an unshared cp.async read stream with eight warps (ldgsts_loaded --table, the other SMs idle); plain stores to fresh destinations on ek4 ek8 ekall g1kall and reads with four warps on g1k8 g1kall ek8 ekall are reported. Quantities: store rate of an SM = box bytes / its period; read rate of an SM = its bytes per cycle; the rate of a GPC or of the card = the sum over its active SMs; TB/s with the device clock. Derivations fixed here, per kind (plain store, reduce store, read) and device: u = the per-SM rate of g1k2. GPC limit W_g = the GPC rate of g1kall, accepted as a limit only if its per-SM rate is below 0.9 u and the GPC rate of g1k12 is within 10 percent of it (flat); otherwise 'not reached' and the largest GPC rate seen is a lower bound. Card layer: with S = the sum over GPCs of min(W_g, active SMs x u) for ekall (W_g of the largest GPC used for every GPC), a separate card limit exists if the card rate of ekall is below 0.85 S, and its value W_c is that card rate; otherwise the GPC limits alone explain the card. Reduce against plain: if W_g(reduce) / W_g(plain) is within 0.72..0.88 the 1.25 cost of a reduce sector applies to the GPC store service as it does to the SM port; outside that it is reported and not assumed. Runs must agree within 5 percent on every rate used. Predictions from the seen data: h100 plain store W_g about 0.8 TB/s and a card layer at about 3.5 TB/s; b300 plain store W_g about 1.1 TB/s (lightly limited, may come out 'not reached') and a card layer at about 4.2; reads W_g 1.05 / 2.7 TB/s and the card at 0.86 / 0.89 of eight times that, i.e. just above the 0.85 line: no separate card layer for reads, stated as borderline. Use: accepted W_g and W_c become candidates for per-GPC rate fields next to the card-wide rates of memory.shared_service (evidence experimental). They are installed only together with an engine rule that puts a per-GPC service in series with the card-wide one, and only after the engine reproduces these cells: simulated per-SM rate within 10 percent of hardware on g1kall and ekall for each kind (replay of traced captures of the same binaries). Until then nothing changes in the model. The reduce rules of the branch task/fg-store-dest are decided after the burst cells (next addendum), not here.

addenda.name: gpc_scope_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-line-mem/scope/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-e373fee9, B300 GPU-ca40cb09; 24 store cells and 14 read cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell; reader fg-line-mem/tools/scope_fit.py)
addenda.text: Per-SM rate of two SMs (u), bytes per cycle, both devices: plain store 31.9, reduce store 25.6 (ratio 0.80); read 78.1 h100 / 123.9 b300. h100. Read: one GPC 1.06 TB/s at 8, 12 and all 18 SMs (accepted: limited and flat, runs identical); every SM 7.78 TB/s = 0.92 of the sum of the GPC limits, so the GPC limits explain the card, as predicted (borderline 0.86 predicted, 0.92 measured). Reduce store: one GPC 0.53 TB/s at 12 and at 18 SMs (accepted); every SM 3.28 / 3.33 TB/s = 0.78-0.79 of the sum: a separate card limit. Plain store: one GPC 0.70 / 0.66 TB/s (limited and flat in both runs, but the runs differ by 6.1 percent, over the 5 percent rule: reported as 0.66-0.70, not accepted as a value); every SM 4.23 / 4.18 TB/s = 0.75-0.79 of the sum: a separate card limit near 4.2 TB/s (installed l2_write_bytes_per_ns 3.96; predicted 3.5 from line B's 64-SM cell, which was not at the limit). Reduce / plain GPC limit 0.75, inside 0.72..0.88: the 1.25 cost of a reduce sector applies to the GPC store service too. b300. Read: one GPC 2.79 TB/s at 12 and 20 SMs (accepted); every SM 20.6-20.7 TB/s = 0.93-0.94 of the sum: no separate card limit. Stores: not reached - a whole GPC of 20 SMs stores at 0.91 u (plain 1.18 TB/s, reduce 0.94), every SM at 0.94 u (plain 8.65 TB/s on the card, reduce 6.86); the prediction of a b300 card layer at 4.2 TB/s was wrong (that cell was not limited), and 8.65 is above the installed l2_write_bytes_per_ns 8.04. Reported: plain stores to fresh destinations reach 3.41 TB/s on the h100 card (4.23 resident) and 7.81 on b300 (8.65); reads with four warps reach the same GPC limits (1.06 / 2.74). Candidates by the declared use, none installed (the engine has no per-GPC service yet and the replay check is not done): h100 l2 read 1.06 TB/s per GPC with no card layer needed, h100 store 0.53 TB/s per GPC for reduce (plain 0.66-0.70, consistent with reduce x 1.25 = 0.66) plus a card layer of about 4.2 TB/s; b300 l2 read 2.79 TB/s per GPC; b300 store limits not reached by one store stream per SM.

addenda.name: gpc_scope_replay
addenda.written: after the replays (fg-line-mem/scope-replay; traced captures of the same binaries on both devices, six cells each; reader fg-line-mem/tools/replay_rates.py: per active CTA the bytes issued between its first and last store / async-copy issue over that interval, against the per-SM rates of the untraced cells of gpc_scope run a)
addenda.text: The declared install condition: simulated per-SM rate within 10 percent of hardware on g1kall and ekall for each kind. Engine: a per-GPC L2 read service and a per-GPC store service (memory.shared_service l2_read_gpc_bytes_per_ns / l2_write_gpc_bytes_per_ns, SM topology gpc) in series before the GPU-wide services. Two defects were found and removed before the replay meant anything, both stated because they changed what was compared: (1) the first replays placed CTAs by the separate placement launch, whose CTA-to-SM map differs from the traced launch; in these probes a CTA works or idles by the SM it was traced on, so the working CTAs were scattered over the GPCs - the replays below use the traced SM of each CTA; (2) the capture axis copies_per_group was reset only at ARRIVES, so kernels that group cp.async with commit_group (LDGDEPBAR) counted copies over the whole kernel and every group took the 32-copy value of storage.ldgsts.completion (1425 cycles) - the converter now also resets at LDGDEPBAR (a conversion change that affects every such kernel, checked by its own full-GPU round). Median simulated / hardware per-SM rate, without | with the candidate values (h100 read 1060, store 663 bytes per ns per GPC; b300 read 2790): h100 stores one GPC 1.71 | 1.01, stores every SM 0.98 | 0.98, reads one GPC 3.41 | 1.03, reads every SM 0.95 | 0.95; b300 reads one GPC 1.42 | 0.96, reads every SM 0.91 | 0.92, stores one GPC 1.05 | 1.05, stores every SM 0.91 | 0.91 (no b300 store value). All eight required cells are within 10 percent with the values, so they are installed (experimental): h100 l2_read_gpc_bytes_per_ns 1060 and l2_write_gpc_bytes_per_ns 663, b300 l2_read_gpc_bytes_per_ns 2790. The h100 store value is not the measured plain-store limit (0.66-0.70, runs 6 percent apart, not accepted) but the accepted reduce limit 0.53 x 1.25, decided after the data. Outside the condition and not met: two SMs of one GPC reading with eight warps each - simulated 101.7 / 97.6 bytes per cycle per SM against 78.1 / 124.0 (1.30 / 0.79); that is the per-SM limit of a cp.async stream, which the engine does not have at the measured values (hardware: h100 18.5 / 70.6 / 78.1 at one / four / eight warps, b300 19.5 / 75.9 / 124.3). Not modelled: the card layer of the h100 store service above the installed GPU-wide rate (measured 4.2 TB/s, installed 3.96), the b300 GPU-wide store rate (installed 8.04, measured at least 8.65).

addenda.name: reduce_rule_scope
addenda.written: before the engine has the rule on this branch and before any replay or full-GPU round of it; seen: the measurements above, gpc_scope_result, and line B's report of its two rules (branch task/fg-store-dest: rule A = a reduce sector occupies the SM store port and the GPU-wide store service 1.25 times as long, rule B = the bulk group of a reduce completes no earlier than the DRAM fetch of its destination; full-GPU r26 with both, in which rule B overcounts on kernels - DGF-BF16-NT-ACCC-C04 1.017 -> 1.402 with the wait for the reduce group going from 27 to 1525 cycles per warp against hardware 29688 cycles for the kernel)
addenda.text: Decision of the shared-memory line for the handed-over rules. Rule A is taken, extended to the per-GPC store service: a reduce sector costs sector_cost_ratio (1.25) on the SM store port, on the per-GPC store service and on the GPU-wide store service. Basis: per-SM reduce / plain rate 0.80 on both devices (25.6 / 31.9 bytes per cycle), per-GPC limit ratio 0.75 on h100 (0.53 / 0.66-0.70), inside the range declared in gpc_scope. Rule B is not taken: it holds for a sustained stream to fresh destinations and overcounts on kernels, and the capacity and scope of whatever absorbs a burst of fetches is not measured (burst cells, not yet run). The destination fetch itself stays as the engine already has it (a reduce sector that is not L2-resident is fetched through the shared DRAM read service; the fetched volume matches hardware). Checks fixed here: (1) replay of line B's traced store_dest cells (fg-line-sync/store-dest-replay captures): reduce ring on one SM and on every SM within 10 percent of hardware on h100; on b300 the every-SM ring is not required because the plain every-SM ring is already 15 percent slow there (installed GPU-wide store rate 8.04 TB/s, measured at least 9.2 TB/s with TMA stores and not at a limit); the fresh-destination reduce cells are expected to stay fast (h100 about 0.7 of hardware as with rule A alone) and are reported as the open rule-B question. (2) a full-GPU round against the branch head; reported per kernel family, cycles decide nothing about the rule. If check (1) fails on h100 the rule is not installed.

addenda.name: reduce_rule_scope_result
addenda.written: after the replay (fg-line-mem/red-replay, line B's traced store_dest captures, reader fg-line-sync/tools/dest_cells.py unchanged) and the full-GPU round m5 (fg-line-mem/full-m5, engine b5539cf9 = dbd1d3ef tree)
addenda.text: Check (1), cycles per 16 KiB, simulated without | with the rule | hardware: h100 reduce ring one SM 517.6 | 647.0 | 640.9 (1.01), reduce ring every SM 1079.4 | 1349.2 | 1380.6 (0.98): both within 10 percent, the rule is installed (storage.tma.reduce sector_cost_ratio 1.25 on the SM store port, the per-GPC and the GPU-wide store service; experimental, line B's leaf). b300 reduce ring one SM 509.0 | 636.2 | 640.9 (0.99); every SM 613.0 | 766.2 | 675.4 (1.13, not required: the plain every-SM ring is 15 percent slow there already). Fresh destinations, every SM (the open rule-B question): h100 1349 against 3796 (0.36), b300 766 against 1570 (0.49) - a sustained stream of reduces to non-resident destinations is still far too fast, as expected without the fetch hold; the plain cells are unchanged. Check (2), full GPU against the branch before the rule (m4), 500 cases each, all ok: h100 MAPE 8.08 -> 8.05 percent, P90 17.3 -> 17.1 (10 kernels move more than 2 percent, 8 closer: deepgemm_kgrouped 0.79-0.92 -> 0.82-0.94); b300 8.27 -> 8.14, P90 16.6 -> 16.5 (18 move, 17 closer: DGF-KG-FP8-TN-R05 0.493 -> 0.582, DGF-KG-BF16-TN-R03 0.855 -> 0.918, DGF-FP8-NT-ACCC-C04 0.821 -> 0.878). None of the kernels that rule B pushed to 1.15-1.40 in line B's round moves beyond 0.97 here. Open: the burst cells that would size what absorbs reduce fetches (not run); the b300 GPU-wide store rate.
